Rashi on Keritot 3a:10:1.hebrew: תנא מאי קחשיב - מכדי, אמרן לעיל: מניינא להכי אתא, שאם עשאן כולן כו' — היכי משכחת לה לשלשים וארבע חטאות בחד:
Rashi on Keritot 3a:10:1.english: What is the tanna tallying? - Seeing that we said above: The tally comes for this [purpose] — that if he performed all of them, etc. [in a single lapse of awareness, he is liable for each and every one] — how can you find [a case of] thirty-four sin offerings in a single [person]?

Rashi on Keritot 3a:11:1.english: A man - He is the one who copulates with an animal.

Rashi on Keritot 3a:11:2.hebrew: איתתא - כגון שנבעלה לבנה, ולבן בעלה, ולחמיה, ולחתנה, ולבהמה — וכן כולם:
Rashi on Keritot 3a:11:2.english: A woman - For example, where she engaged in intercourse with her son, and with her husband’s son, and with her father-in-law, and with her son-in-law, and with an animal — and similarly all of them.

Rashi on Keritot 3a:11:3.hebrew: הבא על הזכור ועל הבהמה - דאין כאן צד אשה. פסח ומילה לא מצי למיפרך, דלאו משום חטאות נקט להו, דהא לאו בני קרבן נינהו, דאין קרבן אלא על לאו, כדמפרש לקמן:
Rashi on Keritot 3a:11:3.english: One who engages in intercourse with a male or with an animal - For there is no aspect of a woman here. [The Gemara] could not object from the Paschal offering and circumcision, for [the Tanna] did not include them on account of sin offerings, as they are not subject to an offering, for an offering is [brought] only for [violating] a negative commandment, as is explained later.

Rashi on Keritot 3a:12:1.english: And it is [in accordance with] Rabbi Yishmael - [This is stated] in chapter Arba Mitot [Sanhedrin 54b].

Rashi on Keritot 3a:13:1.hebrew: והא מדקתני - בכלל כריתות מגדף, לאשמועינן דמביא קרבן, ומוקמי לה לקמן כר״ע, דאמר בסוף פירקין (כריתות דף ז.) מגדף מביא קרבן — רישא נמי ר״ע:
Rashi on Keritot 3a:13:1.english: But from the fact that [the mishna] teaches - [The mishna includes] a blasphemer among [those liable to] karet to teach us that he brings an offering, and we establish it later in accordance with Rabbi Akiva, who says at the end of our chapter (Keritot 7a): "A blasphemer brings an offering" — the first clause is also [in accordance with] Rabbi Akiva.

Rashi on Keritot 3a:14:1.hebrew: דאמר רבי אבהו - בפרק ד' מיתות (סנהדרין נד:): "לא יהיה קדש" — אזהרה לנשכב, ועונש — מגזירה שוה, דכתיב: "וגם קדש היה בארץ". ואי קשיא: גבי עריות היכן מצינו אזהרה לאשה כמו לזכר, דאשכחן בכולהו לאו? פריק הכי: שאני התם, כיון דאיהי נמי מיתהנייא משכיבה, קרינא בה "הנפשות העושות"; אבל משכב זכר, דלא מתהני, בעי אזהרה. ובגברי כתיב, דאין זכור לבהמה, ולא מיקרי קדישות:
Rashi on Keritot 3a:14:1.english: As Rabbi Abbahu says - In chapter Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 54b): “There shall not be a sodomite [kadesh]” (Deuteronomy 23:18) is the warning for the passive partner [the one lain with], and [the] punishment [is derived] from a verbal analogy [gezeirah shavah], as it is written: “And there were also sodomites [kadesh] in the land” (I Kings 14:24). And if [one should] ask: Regarding [other] forbidden relations [arayot], where do we find a warning for the woman comparable to [that for] the male, seeing that we find in all of them a negative commandment [applying to her]? One resolves it thus: It is different there: since she too derives pleasure from the intercourse, we apply to her [the verse]: “the souls that commit them” (Leviticus 18:29); but in [passive] homosexual intercourse, where [the passive partner] does not derive pleasure, he requires [a separate] warning. And [furthermore, “There shall not be a sodomite”] is written regarding men, for [the designation of] “male” does not apply to an animal, and it is not called kedeshut [sodomy].

Rashi on Keritot 3a:18:1.hebrew: ר"א אמר - בגברי חשיב. ודקא קשיא לך דאשה נרבעת — תנא ל"ג חטאות חשיב בחד גברא בהעלם אחד, ותנא אשה נרבעת, ופסח ומילה, לסיומינהו לכריתות:
Rashi on Keritot 3a:18:1.english: Rabbi Elazar said - [He too holds that the Tanna] is counting [cases applicable to] men. And as for that which was difficult to you regarding a woman who submits to bestiality — the Tanna counted thirty-three sin offerings [that can be incurred] by a single man in a single lapse of awareness, and he taught [the cases of] a woman who submits to bestiality, and the Paschal offering and circumcision, to complete [the tally of thirty-six] keritot.

Rashi on Keritot 3a:1:1.hebrew: שאין עונשין מן הדין - דלא אמרינן: מה אחותו מן האב גרידא או מן האם גרידתא ענש עליה — מן האב ומן האם, לא כ"ש:
Rashi on Keritot 3a:1:1.english: That one does not administer punishment based on an inference - For we do not say: Just as [for] his sister from the father alone or from the mother alone, [the Torah] imposed punishment for her — [for his sister] from the father and from the mother, is it not all the more so?

Rashi on Keritot 3a:20:1.english: But the soul that does with a high hand - The verse is speaking of idolatry.

Rashi on Keritot 3a:21:1.hebrew: מה עבודת כוכבים שב ואל תעשה - וחייבין על זדונו כרת, ועל שגגתו חטאת, כדכתיב לעיל מיניה: עז בת שנתה לחטאת:
Rashi on Keritot 3a:21:1.english: Just as idol worship is [a prohibition of] "sit and refrain from action" - And one is liable to *karet* for its intentional [violation] and a sin offering for its unwitting [violation], as it is written prior to it: "A she-goat in its first year for a sin offering."

Rashi on Keritot 3a:21:2.english: So too, every [prohibition of] “sit and refrain from action” - Whose intentional [violation entails] karet and whose unwitting [violation entails] a sin offering.

Rashi on Keritot 3a:23:1.english: They are forty-less-one - Let [the mishna] teach seventy-five [cases of] karet.

Rashi on Keritot 3a:23:2.english: [The tanna] taught [a case of] an unwitting [transgression regarding] Shabbat - For he thought that today was a weekday.

Rashi on Keritot 3a:2:1.hebrew: אי בעית אימא - לר"י אין עונשין מן הדין, ועונש באחותו מן האב ומן האם לר' יצחק נפקא ליה דיליף עונש מאזהרה: כשם שהזהיר עליה כשאר עריות, כך ענש עליה. ואזהרה דידה מפרש במסכת מכות (דף יד.), דאמר קרא: ״ערות בת אביך או בת אמך״ — אין לי אלא בת אביך שלא בת אמך, ובת אמך שלא בת אביך; בת אביך ואמך מנין? ת"ל: ״אחותך היא לא תגלה ערותה״. וכשם שהזהיר עליה, כך ענש עליה:
Rashi on Keritot 3a:2:1.english: And if you wish, say - According to Rabbi Yitzḥak, one does not administer punishment based on an [a fortiori] inference; and the punishment for [intercourse with] his sister from [both] the father and the mother is derived by Rabbi Yitzḥak [from the fact] that he derives punishment from warning: Just as [the Torah] warned concerning her like the other forbidden relations, so it punished for her. And the warning concerning her is explained in Tractate Makkot (14a), where Scripture states: “The nakedness of your father’s daughter or your mother’s daughter” — I have [derived] only the daughter of your father who is not the daughter of your mother, and the daughter of your mother who is not the daughter of your father; from where [is it derived for] the daughter of your father and your mother? The verse states: “She is your sister, you shall not uncover her nakedness.” And just as [the Torah] warned concerning her, so it punished for her.

Rashi on Keritot 3a:3:1.hebrew: א"ר אלעזר חלוק חטאות - שאם עשאן שניהם בהעלם אחת, חייב שתים:
Rashi on Keritot 3a:3:1.english: Rabbi Elazar said: Division of sin offerings - That if he performed both of them in one lapse of awareness, he is liable [to bring] two [sin offerings].

Rashi on Keritot 3a:4:1.english: Karet in [the case of] his sister - Which the verse singled out in her case — for what did it come?

Rashi on Keritot 3a:4:2.hebrew: הגה"ה - כיון דלאוין מחלקין, לא מיבעי ליה לחלק על אחותו שהיא אחות אביו ואחות אמו, שהרי יש בה ג' לאוין:
Rashi on Keritot 3a:4:2.english: Gloss - Since [separate] prohibitions divide [liability], [the verse] is not needed to divide [liability] for his sister who is his father's sister and his mother's sister, for behold, there are three prohibitions [applicable] to her.

Rashi on Keritot 3a:4:3.hebrew: ה"ג: לר' יצחק כדאית ליה, לרבנן מיבעי להו לאחותו בת אביו ואמו, לומר שאין עונשין מן הדין - וכוליה קרא משום אחותו דסיפא אתא, ובשביל חדוש אחד דרך לשנות פרשה שנאמרה:
Rashi on Keritot 3a:4:3.english: This is the reading: According to Rabbi Yitzḥak, as he holds; according to the Rabbis, they require it for his sister [who is] the daughter of his father and his mother, to say that one does not administer punishment based on an [a fortiori] inference - And the entire verse came [only] because of “his sister” in the latter clause; and for the sake of one novel point, it is [Scripture’s] way to repeat a passage that was [already] stated.

Rashi on Keritot 3a:4:4.hebrew: לרבי יצחק מיבעי ליה כו' עד סיפא - ל"ג לה, ופירוש משובש הוא מתלמידים טועין. עד כאן הגה"ה:
Rashi on Keritot 3a:4:4.english: “According to Rabbi Yitzḥak, he requires it, etc.,” until the end - We do not read it, and it is an erroneous explanation from mistaken students. Until here is the gloss.

Rashi on Keritot 3a:8:1.hebrew: וחייבין עליהן בפני עצמה - על כל אחד, כי עביד להו בהעלם אחת:
Rashi on Keritot 3a:8:1.english: And one is liable for them by itself - For each one, when he performed them in a single lapse of awareness.
